Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:10:1.hebrew: רישא נותן לו כשעת הנזק - ולא מצי א"ל מאי אפסדתיך, בין דפטומי פטמיה בין דשבח ממילא. והיכא דפטמיה לא הוה אצטריך למיתנא, אלא משום היכא דשבח ממילא אצטריך לאשמועינן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:10:1.english: [In] the first clause, he gives him [compensation] according to the time of the injury - and he cannot say to him, "What loss did I cause you?" — whether he fattened it or whether it appreciated by itself. And where he fattened it, it would not have been necessary to teach [this]; rather, because of [the case] where it appreciated by itself, it was necessary to teach us [this].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:11:1.english: [If] it depreciated, [it is evaluated] according to the time of standing trial - [It] refers back to the first clause.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:13:1.english: And they shall divide its money - That is, half-damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:14:1.hebrew: וכן הלכה - ודאי כן הלכה, דמנה נותן לו, דהיינו ח"נ; אבל אין זה שור האמור בתורה, דקיימת "ומכרו את השור החי וגו'". ובגמ' מפרש במאי פליגי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:14:1.english: And so is the halakha - Certainly so is the halakha, that he gives him a maneh [one hundred dinars], which is half-damages; however, this is not the ox stated in the Torah, for you have fulfilled [only], "Then they shall sell the live ox, etc." And in the Gemara it explains regarding what they disagree.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:14:2.hebrew: והנבילה יפה נ' זוז - דה"ל הזיקו ק"נ, ופלגא נזקא — דהיינו ע"ה — בעי ניזק להפסיד. והלכך, שקיל חצי (נזק) החי וחצי המת דשוו קכ"ה, ומטי לכל אחד פסידא ע"ה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:14:2.english: And the carcass is worth fifty zuz - For its damage is one hundred and fifty [zuz], and half the damage — which is seventy-five [zuz] — the injured party must lose. Therefore, he takes half of the live [ox] and half of the dead [ox], which are worth one hundred and twenty-five [zuz], and a loss of seventy-five [zuz] falls to each one.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:16:1.hebrew: פחת שפחתתו מיתה מחצין בחי - כלומר, נבילה לא שייכא גבי מזיק כלל, אלא שמין את הנבילה כמה פחותין דמיה עכשיו משעה שהיה חי, ונותן לו מזיק חצי הפחת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:16:1.english: [The] depreciation that death caused it, they divide in the live [ox] - That is to say, the carcass does not pertain to the damager at all; rather, they appraise the carcass [to see] how much less its value is now than when it was alive, and the damager gives him half of the depreciation.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:18:1.hebrew: פחת נבילה - אם פחתו דמיה משעת מיתה עד שעת מכירה, לר"מ דאמר לא שייך מזיק בנבילה, פחת דניזק הוי, ולא יהיב ליה אלא חצי מה שפחתה מיתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:18:1.english: The diminishing [value] of the carcass - If its value diminished from the time of death until the time of sale, according to Rabbi Meir, who says [that] the damager has no share in the carcass, the depreciation belongs to the injured party, and he gives him only half of what [its value] diminished [due to] death.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:1:1.hebrew: ואפי' הזיק עד שלא חב - נמי בעל חוב קדים לתפיסה, וכיון דתפס, אמאי מפקינן מיניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:1:1.english: And even [if] it caused damage before he incurred the debt - [here] too, the creditor was first to seize [it]; and since he seized [it], why do we take [it] away from him?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:1:2.hebrew: ש"מ - בתמיה, דפלוגתא היא בעלמא (כתובות דף צד.), דאיכא למ"ד מה שגבה גבה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:1:2.english: Conclude from it - [This is said] as a rhetorical question, for it is a dispute elsewhere (Ketubot 94a), as there is one who says [that] what he collected, he has collected.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:1:3.hebrew: אית דגרסי ואפי' הזיק עד שלא חב נמי דניזק קדים ש"מ כו' - כלומר, אע"ג דניזק קדים שיעבודיה, קשיא ליה האי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:1:3.english: Some have the reading: And even [if] it caused damage before he owed, [where] the injured party preceded as well, conclude from this, etc. - That is to say, even though the injured party's lien preceded [that of the creditor], this [question] is [still] difficult for him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:2:1.english: If it had been in your possession - [Meaning,] that you had already collected it before it caused damage.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:2:2.english: Am I not paid from you - [This is] a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:3:1.hebrew: ושבח - ניזק, ועמד על ד' מאות זוז:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:3:1.english: And it appreciated - [The] injured [ox], and [it] stood at four hundred zuz.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:3:2.hebrew: שאלמלא כו' - כלומר, הועיל ואיכא למימר אלמלא לא הזיקו היה עומד על שמונה מאות זוז, נותן לו כ"ה זוזים כשעת הנזק; ולא מצי א"ל: "מאי אפסדתיך, הא שבח טפי?", משום דאמר ליה ניזק: "אי לא אזיקתן, הוי שבח וקאי על תמני מאה". ל"א: שאלמלא לא הזיקו כו', ועכשיו תובע ניזק מאתים — חציין של ד' מאות, חצי נזק שהפסידו — אינו נותן לו אלא כ"ה כשעת הנזק. וראשון עיקר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:3:2.english: For if [it had] not, etc. - That is to say, since one can say [that] had it not injured it, it would have stood at eight hundred zuz, [the owner of the goring ox] gives him twenty-five zuz according to [its value at] the time of the injury. And he cannot say to him, "What loss did I cause you? Behold, it appreciated even more!" — because the injured party says to him, "Had you not injured it, it would have appreciated and stood at eight hundred." Another version: "For had it not injured it, etc.," and now the injured party claims two hundred — half of four hundred, [which is] half the damage that it caused him to lose — [nevertheless,] he gives him only twenty-five [zuz] according to [its value at] the time of the injury. And the first [explanation] is the primary one.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:4:1.hebrew: כיחש - הניזק מחמת המכה, ונראה עכשיו הזיקו גדול יותר מתחילה בשעת הנזק, נותן לו כפי נזק שבשעת העמדה בדין, כדקאמר לקמן, "קרנא דתורך קבירא ביה":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:4:1.english: Depreciated - [If] the injured [ox depreciated] due to the blow, and its damage now appears greater than [it did] initially at the time of the injury, he pays him according to the damage [evaluated] at the time of standing trial, as [the Gemara] says below: "The horn of your ox is buried in it."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:5:1.hebrew: שבח מזיק - ועמד על ד' מאות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:5:1.english: [If the ox] that caused the injury appreciated - and stood at four hundred [zuz].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:5:2.hebrew: נותן לו - כ"ה זוז כשעת הנזק, ואין יכול ניזק לומר לו: "תן לי חלק שמינית שבו, שזכיתי בו משעת הנזק וברשותי השביח":
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:5:2.english: He gives him - Twenty-five zuz, according to [its value at] the time of the injury; and the injured party cannot say to him, "Give me an eighth share of it, for I acquired it from the time of the injury and it appreciated in my possession."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:7:1.hebrew: כחש כשעת העמדה בדין - ונותן לו חלק שמינית שבו, שברשותו כחש. ולקמן פריך רישא לסיפא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:7:1.english: [If it] depreciated, [it is evaluated] as of the time of standing trial - And he gives him an eighth share of it, for it depreciated while in his [the damager's] possession. And later [the Gemara] raises a difficulty [regarding] the first clause [versus] the latter clause.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:8:1.hebrew: ה"ג כולה ר' עקיבא היא וכשפיטמו - מזיק לשור, וחסר ממונו לשבוחיה, הלכך לא שקיל ניזק בשבחא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:8:1.english: This is the reading: It is all [the opinion of] Rabbi Akiva, and where [he] fattened it - [That is,] the damager [fattened] the ox, and spent his own money to improve it; therefore, the injured party does not take [a share] in the appreciation.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:9:1.hebrew: אימא רישא שיבח ניזק ועמד על ארבע מאות זוז - אפי' הכי נותן לו כשעת הנזק, ולא מצי א"ל: מאי אפסדתיך? משום דא"ל ניזק: אלמלא לא הזיקו, היה עומד על ח' מאות:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:9:1.english: Say the first clause: [If] the injured [ox] appreciated and stood at four hundred zuz - Even so, [the damager] pays him according to [its value at] the time of the injury, and he cannot say to him, "What loss have I caused you?" because the injured party says to him, "Had he not injured it, it would have stood at eight hundred [zuz]."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:9:2.hebrew: ואי כשפיטמו - ניזק לשורו, צריכא למימר דיהיב לו כשעת הנזק? ולא מצי א"ל: מאי אפסדתיך? הא האי דאשבח, משום פיטומו הוא, וחסר ביה ממונא. ללישנא אחרינא הכי משמע: אימא רישא: שבח ניזק, נותן לו כשעת הנזק ותו לא, ולא מצי למימר ניזק: תן לי ב' מאות, שאלמלא לא הזיקו כו'. ואי בשפיטמו ניזק, צריכא למימר דלא יהיב ליה מזיק ב' מאות? האי דאשבח, משום פיטומא הוא! וקשיא לי: הא ודאי אצטריך לאשמועינן, דאשתבח דאפסדיה, דאי לא אזיק הוה קאי השתא בהאי פיטומא דפטמיה על תמני מאה. ולשון ראשון שמעתי, ועיקר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 34a:9:2.english: And if [it is] where he fattened it - [i.e.,] the injured party [fattened] his ox, need it be said that [the damager] gives him [compensation] according to [its value at] the time of the injury? And [the damager] cannot say to him, "What loss did I cause you?" [For] that which it appreciated [in value] is due to his fattening [of it], and he expended money on it. According to another version, this is what it means: Say the first clause: [If] the injured [ox] appreciated, he gives him [compensation] according to [its value at] the time of the injury and no more, and the injured party cannot say, "Give me two hundred [dinars], for had it not injured it, etc." And if [it is] where the injured party fattened it, need it be said that the damager does not give him two hundred [dinars]? That which it appreciated is due to the fattening! However, this is difficult for me: Surely this would indeed need to be taught to us, for [even as] it appreciated, he caused him a loss, since had it not been injured, it would now stand, through this fattening with which he fattened it, at eight hundred [dinars]! And the first version is what I heard [from my teachers], and [it is] the authoritative [one].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:14:1.hebrew: זה נוטל חצי החי וחצי המת - האי לישנא לאו דוקא, ולא אתי למימר אלא שמקבל עליו חצי הפחת, ולפי המסקנא שקיל בשבחא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:14:1.english: "This [party] takes half of the living [ox] and half of the dead [ox]" - This wording is not exact, and it only comes to say that [the damager] accepts upon himself half of the depreciation [of the carcass], and according to the conclusion [of the Gemara], he [also] takes [a share] in the appreciation [of the carcass].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:18:1.hebrew: דרבי מאיר סבר פחת נבלה דניזק - אע"ג דבפ"ק (ד' י:) נפקא לן מ"והמת יהיה לו", מ"מ האי קרא דהכא אצטריך לאשמועינן דלא משלם אלא חצי נזק; דאי מ"וחצו את כספו", ה"א שהוא פעמים יותר ופעמים פחות, כדמוכח בסמוך דפריך: "א"כ מצינו תם לר' יהודה דמשלם יותר מח"נ", ומשני: "אית ליה לרבי יהודה פחת שפחתו מיתה מחצין". אלמא נפקא לן מ"וגם את המת יחצון" דלא משלם אלא חצי נזק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:18:1.english: [That] Rabbi Meir holds [that] the diminishing [value] of the carcass is the injured party's - Even though in the first chapter (10b) we derive [this] from "and the dead [animal] shall be his," nevertheless this verse here is needed to teach us that [the damager] pays only half-damages; for if [we derived it only] from "and they shall divide its money," I would have thought that it is sometimes more and sometimes less [than half-damages], as is evident immediately below, where [the Gemara] asks: "If so, we find a tam [innocuous ox] according to Rabbi Yehuda that pays more than half-damages," and [the Gemara] answers: "Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] the depreciation that death caused it, they divide." Thus we see that we derive from "and also the dead [animal] they shall divide" that he pays only half-damages.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:2:1.hebrew: אילו גבך הוה לאו מינך הוה גבי ליה - תימה: אז הוא בדין שיגבה, שפשע בשמירתו! וי"ל דלא קאמר אלא כלומר דאין גוף השור משועבד לב"ח, כמו שהוא משועבד לניזק שמשתלם מגופו. וכן פירש בקונטרס בריש שור שנגח ארבעה וחמשה (לקמן בבא קמא ד' לו.):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:2:1.english: "If it had been in your possession, would he not have collected it from you?" - This is astonishing! Then it would be right that he should collect [from you], because [the possessor] was negligent in guarding it! And one can say [in answer] that [the Gemara] is only saying, as it were, that the body of the ox is not encumbered to a creditor in the way that it is encumbered to an injured party, who is paid from its very body. And so Rashi explained at the beginning of [the chapter] Shor SheNagach Arba'ah VeChamishah (later, Bava Kamma 36a).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:3:1.hebrew: שאלמלא לא הזיקו היה עומד על שמנה מאות זוז נותן כשעת הנזק - לא נקטיה לאשמועינן שלא ישלם כל מה שהיה ראוי להשביח אלמלא לא הוזק, דמילתא דפשיטא הוא; דאטו אם נגח שור קטן, הייתי סבור שישלם דמי שור גדול לפי שהיה ראוי להיות גדול ומשביח? ועוד, אי להכי אצטריך, מאי פריך בסמוך: "אי כשפטמו, צריכא למימר"? אלא י"ל כפי' הקונט' בלשון אחר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:3:1.english: "If it had not injured it, it would have stood at eight hundred zuz; he gives [compensation] as at the time of the injury" - [The Baraita] did not state [this] to teach us that he does not pay all that [the ox] would have been fit to appreciate had it not been injured, for that is an obvious matter; could it be that if [an ox] gored a small ox, I would think that he should pay the value of a large ox because it was fit to grow large and appreciate? And furthermore, if it was needed for that [purpose], what does [the Gemara] ask immediately below: "If [it refers to] when he fattened it, why is it necessary to state [this]?" Rather, one must say like Rashi's explanation in the other version.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:8:1.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן כשפטמו - וכגון שאין השבח יותר על היציאה, שאם היה יותר — נהי נמי דאמרינן בחזקת הבתים (ב"ב ד' מב:) דשותף הוי כיורד ברשות, מ"מ מה שאדם רוצה ליתן למפטם לפטם יטול המזיק, והמותר יש לו להיות לניזק. וא"ת: א"כ, אמאי אצטריך למיפרך מרישא? מסיפא גופה לפרוך: "אי בשפטמו, צריכא למימר?" וי"ל: דסיפא אצטריך, דסד"א כיון דאמר ר"ע הוחלט השור, הוי ליה מזיק כשפטמו מניח מעותיו על קרן הצבי, כמו בהלך למדינת הים ובא אחר ופרנס אשתו (כתובות ד' קז:). ועוד מצינו למימר: דאיירי שפיר שהשבח יתר על היציאה, והא דקאמר "נותן כשעת הנזק" לאו דוקא, אלא בא להשמיענו שיטול יותר מדמי יציאותיו, דכיורד ברשות דמי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:8:1.english: Here, with what are we dealing? Where he fattened it. - And [this is] in a case where the appreciation is not greater than the expenditure. For if it were greater — even though we say in [the chapter] Chezkas HaBatim (Bava Batra 42b) that a partner is like one who enters [another's property] with permission, nevertheless, [only] what a person is willing to give to a fattener to fatten [the animal] shall the damager take, and the remainder must belong to the injured party. And if you ask: If so, why was it necessary [for the Gemara] to challenge from the first clause? From the latter clause itself it should have challenged: "If [it is] where he fattened it, need it be said?" And one can answer: The latter clause is necessary, for it might have entered your mind to say that since Rabbi Akiva said the ox is transferred [to the injured party], the damager, when he fattens it, is like one who places his money on the horn of a deer [i.e., forfeits his expenses], like in [the case of] one who went overseas and another came and sustained his wife (Ketubot 107b). And furthermore, we can say that it is indeed speaking [of a case] where the appreciation is greater than the expenditure, and that which it says, "he gives [according to] the time of the injury," is not meant literally; rather, it comes to teach us that [the damager] takes more than the value of his expenditures, for he is like one who enters with permission.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:8:2.hebrew: כשפיטמו - וא"ת: אמאי מפליג בין שבח לכחש, לפלוג בשבח גופיה — דשבח ממילא כשעת העמדה בדין? וי"ל: דאגב דנקט ברישא שבח וכחש, בסיפא נמי נקט הכי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 34a:8:2.english: "When he fattened it" - And if you ask: Why does [the baraita] distinguish between appreciation and depreciation? Let it distinguish within appreciation itself — that [when] it appreciated on its own, [it is assessed] as of the time of standing in court! And one can say [in answer]: Since it stated "appreciation and depreciation" in the first clause, in the latter clause as well it stated it this way.
